question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, egress 205.188.204.187
request.body: a keyless MCP initialize and tools/list on the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, then a tools/call naming microsoft_docs_fetch, the tool name written into the description of the search tool this endpoint serves. All three answered 200. Accept application/json and text/event-stream

decoded.the-endpoint-is-documented: the vendor's repository README reads "For applications that require OpenAI Deep Research model compatibility, you can use the OpenAI-compatible endpoint: https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp/openai-compatible". The release notes date it 2025-12-10
decoded.keyless-and-the-same-server: initialize answers 200 with no credentials, serverInfo Microsoft Learn MCP Server 1.0.0, the same four advertised capabilities as the main endpoint. Its instructions string says "via two tools" and heads them search and fetch
decoded.two-tools-different-names: tools/list serves exactly two: search (required [query], properties [query]) and fetch (required [id], properties [id]). The main endpoint's three are microsoft_docs_search, microsoft_code_sample_search and microsoft_docs_fetch, and its fetch tool takes url, not id
decoded.the-descriptions-name-tools-that-are-not: search's own description contains "## Follow-up Pattern To ensure completeness, use microsoft_docs_fetch when high-value pages are identified by search." fetch's description contains "## Usage Pattern Use this tool AFTER microsoft_docs_search when you identify specific high-value pages". Both names are quoted verbatim from the tools/list response of this endpoint, archived in full in the artifact's appendix M.2
decoded.and-they-are-not-callable-here: tools/call of microsoft_docs_fetch on this endpoint answers {"error":{"code":-32602,"message":"Unknown tool: 'microsoft_docs_fetch'"}} inside HTTP 200, at 12:23:21Z in the second reading
decoded.one-more-contract-difference: search on this endpoint REQUIRES query; microsoft_docs_search on the main endpoint declares no required array and answers an empty-argument call with empty results (p-20260930-microsoft-learn-mcp-refusals-as-success). Same function, two contracts
decoded.two-readings: two readings on 2026-09-30, the second a re-run of this record's own published command with the response date header captured per request: the first pass ran from 12:03:48Z (the date header of its initialize) to before 12:18Z, and only that first response's clock time was captured, which is why this record's at is the SECOND reading's instant. Every value below reproduced in the second pass (artifact section N)
decoded.not-measured: whether an OpenAI Deep Research client is affected in practice, since such a client may be told the tool names out of band. The byte-identical descriptions show the strings are shared; they do not show where in the vendor's code the sharing happens, and this record does not guess.
decoded.the-descriptions-are-byte-identical-acro: measured, not inferred: microsoft_docs_search's description on the main endpoint and search's description here are the same 716 bytes and compare equal; microsoft_docs_fetch's and fetch's are the same 1065 bytes and compare equal. The title fields match too ("Microsoft Docs Search", "Microsoft Docs Fetch"). So the two endpoints serve one set of description strings under two sets of names, and only the name and the argument key were changed for OpenAI compatibility. That is why the text points at names this endpoint does not serve.

finding: On the OpenAI-compatible endpoint Microsoft documents for Deep Research clients, keyless on 2026-09-30, tools/list serves two tools named search and fetch. The description of search tells the caller to follow up with microsoft_docs_fetch, and the description of fetch points back at microsoft_docs_search. Neither name exists on that endpoint: a tools/call of microsoft_docs_fetch there answers JSON-RPC -32602 "Unknown tool". An agent that follows the follow-up pattern written into the tool it just called issues a call that cannot succeed. The argument names differ too: fetch takes id where the main endpoint's microsoft_docs_fetch takes url, and search requires query where microsoft_docs_search does not. The description strings are byte-identical to their main-endpoint counterparts (716 and 1065 bytes, comparing equal), so the two endpoints serve one set of descriptions under two sets of names.
